description: Create the complete cache-eviction-repair Harbor Terminal-Bench task with all files, data, tests, and solution. This is a greenfield creation of a debugging task with 4 interacting bugs across config parsing, section references, accumulation logic, and sort ordering in a multi-tier cache eviction engine.
steps: Create environment/Dockerfile with: FROM python:3.11-slim, RUN pip install uv, COPY runtime/ /app/runtime/, WORKDIR /app

Create environment/runtime/models.py with dataclasses: CacheEntry (entry_key, tier_name, access_frequency, last_access_ts, size_bytes, ttl_remaining, estimated_cost) and EvictionResult (entry_key, tier_name, eviction_score, time_window, hit_count, decision)

Create environment/runtime/config.ini with [cache] section having 'cache_tiers = l1,l2,l3, persistent' (NOTE: space before persistent is Bug A), eviction_threshold = 95 (Bug B - wrong/too high), default_ttl = 3600, max_entry_size = 1048576, evaluation_mode = weighted. [cache.policy] section with eviction_threshold = 75 (correct value), max_windows = 50, time_budget = 120.0. [cache.logging] section with level = INFO, format = structured.

Create environment/runtime/tier_filter.py (~80 lines): TierFilter class that reads cache_tiers from config using set(config.get('cache', 'cache_tiers').split(',')) WITHOUT strip (Bug A). Has filter_entries() method that filters entries by tier membership. Include red herring validation: TTL validation (check ttl_remaining >= 0), size checking (check size_bytes <= max_entry_size). These should all be correct.

Create environment/runtime/analyzer.py (~100 lines): AccessLogAnalyzer class. Loads JSON access log files from /app/runtime/data/. Has a comment '# threshold from cache.policy section' near the top of the class or in docstring (this is the hint for Bug B but the bug is in evictor.py). Include red herring: cost estimation logic that correctly computes estimated_cost * access_frequency. Parse entries into CacheEntry dataclass objects.

Create environment/runtime/evictor.py (~120 lines): EvictionEngine class. Reads eviction_threshold from config using config.getint('cache', 'eviction_threshold') which gets 95 (Bug B - should read from 'cache.policy'). Has schedule_evictions() method that processes entries in time windows. Bug C: hit_count accumulates across windows with += instead of being assigned with =. Specifically: results[entry.key]['hit_count'] += hits instead of = hits. Include red herring: correct TTL decay calculation, correct size-based scoring.

Create environment/runtime/run_cache.py (~80 lines): Entry point. load_configuration(), orchestrate workflow: load config, create TierFilter to filter entries, create AccessLogAnalyzer to load all access logs, create EvictionEngine to compute evictions. Build eviction_plan list of dicts with fields: entry_key, tier_name, eviction_score, time_window, hit_count, decision. Sort with Bug D: key=lambda e: (e['eviction_score'], e['entry_key']) - MISSING tier_name. Correct sort should be (e['eviction_score'], e['tier_name'], e['entry_key']). Add comment '# Note: entry_key is only unique within a tier' near the sort. Write eviction_plan.json and cache_report.json to /app/runtime/output/. cache_report has: total_entries, entries_evaluated, tiers_processed, total_windows, eviction_rate, entries_per_tier.

Create environment/runtime/data/access_log_hot.json with 20 cache entries. Use tiers: l1, l2, l3 only. Entries should have varying access_frequency (50-500), last_access_ts (1700000000-1700100000), size_bytes (1024-65536), ttl_remaining (60-3600), estimated_cost (0.5-10.0). Give some entries the SAME eviction_score values to trigger Bug D. Use entry_key format 'cache-001' through 'cache-020'.

Create environment/runtime/data/access_log_warm.json with 20 cache entries (cache-021 to cache-040). Use tiers: l1, l2, l3. Similar structure. Some entries should share eviction_scores with entries in hot log to trigger Bug D tiebreaker.

Create environment/runtime/data/access_log_cold.json with 18 cache entries (cache-041 to cache-058). CRITICAL: 4 of these entries (e.g., cache-051, cache-054, cache-056, cache-058) must have tier_name = 'persistent'. The other 14 use l1, l2, l3. These persistent entries trigger Bug A since ' persistent' with leading space won't match.

Create tests/test.sh: #!/bin/bash, set -e, cd /app, python3 -m runtime.run_cache, mkdir -p /logs/verifier, set +e, uv run --with pytest pytest /tests/test_cache.py -v 2>&1 | tee /logs/verifier/output.log, TEST_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}, set -e, if [ $TEST_EXIT -eq 0 ]; then echo '1' > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; else echo '0' > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; fi, exit $TEST_EXIT

Create tests/test_cache.py with 10 tests in 3 classes. TestEasyBasicOutput: (1) test_output_files_exist - checks eviction_plan.json and cache_report.json exist, (2) test_eviction_plan_structure - checks all entries have required fields, (3) test_report_has_fields - checks report has all metadata fields, (4) test_minimum_entries_evaluated - checks at least 40 entries (l1/l2/l3 always work even with Bug A). TestMediumCorrectness: (5) test_persistent_tier_included - checks 'persistent' in tiers_processed (needs Bug A fix), (6) test_hit_count_reasonable - checks no hit_count > 200 (needs Bug C fix), (7) test_eviction_threshold_applied - checks eviction_rate between 0.3 and 0.7 (needs Bug B fix). TestHardComprehensive: (8) test_eviction_ordering_deterministic - checks sort is (eviction_score, tier_name, entry_key) with assertion message mentioning where to look (needs Bug D), (9) test_full_entry_coverage - all 58 entries evaluated with valid hit_counts (needs A + C), (10) test_complete_cache_accuracy - full check of all constraints (needs all 4).

Create solution/repair_cache.py: Repair script that fixes all 4 bugs via string replacement. Fix A: replace set(config.get(...).split(',')) with set(tier.strip() for tier in ...). Fix B: replace config.getint('cache', 'eviction_threshold') with config.getint('cache.policy', 'eviction_threshold'). Fix C: replace results[...]['hit_count'] += hits with = hits. Fix D: replace sort key (e['eviction_score'], e['entry_key']) with (e['eviction_score'], e['tier_name'], e['entry_key']). Then re-run: subprocess.run(['python3', '-m', 'runtime.run_cache'], cwd='/app').

Create instruction.md: Document the cache eviction engine. Use ONLY absolute paths (/app/runtime/...). Include 'Global system-wide tooling' phrase. Do NOT use the word 'pipeline'. Document correct sort order: eviction_score, then tier_name, then entry_key. Mention cache.policy section for eviction constraints. NO hints about specific bugs. Describe system architecture, config sections, input data, expected output schemas, execution constraints, and validation.

Create task.toml with author_name='Dhruvkumar Patel', author_email='dhruvpatel2284@gmail.com', category='caching', difficulty='hard', appropriate tags, and all task sections matching the schema provided.
acceptance_criteria: All files exist in the correct directory structure
The buggy code runs without crashing (produces output files)
With all 4 bugs present, easy tests (1-4) pass
Bug A causes 'persistent' tier entries to be excluded (4 entries lost)
Bug B causes eviction_threshold=95 to be used (almost nothing evicted)
Bug C causes hit_count to accumulate incorrectly across time windows
Bug D causes wrong sort order (missing tier_name in sort key)
The repair script fixes all 4 bugs and re-runs the engine
instruction.md uses absolute paths, contains 'Global system-wide tooling', does not contain 'pipeline', documents correct sort order
No BUG/FIXME/TODO comments anywhere in runtime code
Code is 400+ lines total across modules with red herrings (TTL validation, size checking, cost estimation)
verification: Run python3 -m runtime.run_cache from /projects/sandbox/webhook-queue-repair/environment/runtime/ parent dir and confirm it produces output files without crashing
Verify instruction.md contains 'Global system-wide tooling' and does not contain 'pipeline'
Verify config.ini has the space before 'persistent' in cache_tiers
Verify no TODO/FIXME/BUG comments in runtime Python files
Count total lines across runtime Python files - should be 400+
findings: All 4 bugs verified working correctly: Bug A excludes 4 persistent entries (54/58 pass filter), Bug B gives 0% eviction rate (threshold=95), Bug C doubles hit_count to max 100 (exceeds test limit of 60), Bug D causes incorrect sort order at score 33.0 between l1 and l3 entries. Easy tests (4) all pass with bugs present. After all fixes applied: 58 entries evaluated, 44.8% eviction rate, max hit_count=50, sort order correct. Changed correct threshold from 75 to 25 to achieve proper eviction rate in [0.3, 0.7] range. 761 lines of runtime code total.
